title: Disrupting the $15 Trillion Construction Industry with Autonomous Agents: Dr. Sarah Buchner
talk_summary: A short vendor pitch from Structurize (Trunk Tools) about putting a RAG 'brain' over millions of pages of construction documents and deploying vertical agents on top to answer field questions and auto-resolve data discrepancies. The only transferable ideas are architectural: a shared domain knowledge base under many specialized agents, and agents that close the loop on detected inconsistencies instead of just reporting them.

takeaways.technique: Shared domain 'brain' as a retrieval layer under all agents
takeaways.what_they_do: Ingest all domain-specific file types into one indexed knowledge store, then have every agent query that store rather than each agent carrying its own context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We are putting all of this knowledge in one place, which is what we call the brain behind construction
takeaways.numbers: 3.6 million pages of documentation for one skyscraper

takeaways.technique: Agents resolve discrepancies, not just report them
takeaways.what_they_do: When the system detects a data inconsistency, an agent drafts the resolution (an RFI) for a human to approve, rather than stopping at the flag.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Instead of stopping where we have the data discrepancies, why don't you use an agent that is just actually an RFI and solving the discrepancy

takeaways.what_they_do: Every semantic answer is returned alongside the original source file so the user can verify the claim.
takeaways.evidence_quote: within a few seconds we give you the enterprise search results and obviously we also give you a semantic answer
